status: v2 structured; scope-dependent classes are DEPENDS_ON_RULING until the user rules on product scope (see reports/go-h1-semantic-decisions.md H1.1). Not preregistration-ready.
purpose: Decide E (eligible PR) from source semantics only. Must not consult oba output, test presence, derivability, or historical verdicts.

scope_readings.a: declared goal: option branch activation (README layer A). Units: option declaration semantics and branch predicates over options. No runtime claim.
scope_readings.b: runtime or public contract. Would extend E beyond layer A and reopen README non-goal 'No claim about runtime behavior'. Not adopted; requires a declared-goal change first.

product_premises.P1: oba's unit is an option's semantics: declaration, default, type, apply/readOnly, and the branch predicates that read the option. Documentation-only fields are outside the unit.
product_premises.P2: Configuration VALUES (config.<path> = ...) are a separate unit (configuration choice). Out of scope for E under reading (a). Separate mode needed.
product_premises.P3: E is not reduced by oba's current coverage. Analyzer inability is an OBA DISCOVERY or OBA ANALYSIS outcome counted after V.

procedure: 1. Take the PR's changed files restricted to nixos/modules/** and nixos/tests/**. Record every hunk.
2. For each hunk, identify the innermost enclosing construct in BASE and HEAD source by parsing, not by line-prefix heuristics.
3. Assign each hunk one class from classes[]. Containment inside mkOption { } alone never makes a hunk eligible; the attribute the changed text belongs to decides (attribute_rule).
4. For each hunk record: operands read (in-module or foreign), the option-contract property changed, and the eligibility under each scope reading.
5. A hunk whose eligibility is DEPENDS_ON_RULING is recorded as such and is not counted as ELIGIBLE or INELIGIBLE. A PR whose only hunks are DEPENDS_ON_RULING has E = PENDING_RULING.
6. A CONDITIONAL hunk (EC10, EC13 where unclear) needs a written reason in the adjudication record; with no reason it is NOT_RESOLVED.
7. Record per PR: R (file-path rule only), E under each reading, the decisive hunk, and one sentence of reason.
8. Do NOT decide D or V here. A PR can be E and still have no mechanically derivable target.

attribute_rule.rule: A change to a behavioral attribute is behavioral. A change to a documentation attribute only is documentation. A change that touches both is behavioral. Attribute attribution uses the innermost attribute key the changed text belongs to.

operand_rule.in_module: the operand is an option declared in the changed module (verified by source search at the same SHA)
operand_rule.foreign: the operand is an option declared in another module
operand_rule.note: A predicate whose only changed operand is foreign is a change to the foreign option's branch, not to this module's option. Under reading (a) it is DEPENDS_ON_RULING (U4), not ELIGIBLE by default.

classes.name: new option declaration
classes.reason: A new option's default and type are new behavior a test can witness.

classes.name: removed option declaration
classes.reason: Removal changes which configurations are accepted and what they do.

classes.name: default value changed
classes.reason: Changes behavior for every configuration that does not set the option.

classes.name: type changed
classes.reason: Changes which values are accepted and how they merge.

classes.name: apply or readOnly changed
classes.reason: Changes the value seen by config or the assignability of the option.

classes.name: example only changed
classes.reason: Documentation attribute; no evaluated behavior. Closes U1.

classes.name: description only changed
classes.reason: Documentation attribute; no evaluated behavior. Closes U1.

classes.name: defaultText only changed
classes.reason: Rendering of the default for documentation only; the default itself is unchanged. Closes U1.

classes.name: formatting, reordering, or comment change inside a declaration
classes.reason: No semantic change to any attribute.

classes.name: default or type expression rewritten, equivalence unknown from syntax
classes.semantic_property: default or type (equivalence to be shown)
classes.reason: Must state whether the evaluated value or accepted set changes. If not: INELIGIBLE with that reason. If yes: ELIGIBLE under EC03/EC04.

classes.name: configuration value assignment (config.<path> = ...) not declared by the PR's own options
classes.reason: Configuration choice, not option semantics (P2). Under (a) no Nix evaluation is claimed, so values are outside E. Under (b) they may be in scope; separate mode needed either way.

classes.name: branch predicate changed that reads an existing option

eligibility.a: ELIGIBLE if the changed predicate's changed operand is in_module; DEPENDS_ON_RULING if the only new operand is foreign

classes.reason: Behavior conditioned on an option. Foreign-only operand cases are the 566007 split.

classes.name: assertion or warning changed

eligibility.b: ELIGIBLE iff the condition reads an option declared in this module; else INELIGIBLE

classes.reason: README layer A defines branches, not assertions or warnings. Reading (b) follows the v1 rule. 566696 warning is EC13 under (b).

classes.name: test-only change (nixos/tests/**, no module behavior hunk)
classes.reason: Changes the witness, not the module's option semantics. Counts for R only.

classes.name: package-only or non-NixOS-module change
classes.reason: Outside the NixOS module unit. Not in census R.

classes.name: rename or move of an option (mkRenamedOptionModule, mkRemovedOptionModule, or explicit relocation)
classes.scope: in_module (old path base, new path head)
classes.side: base for old path, head for new path
classes.reason: Both old and new option paths are the subject; the relocation mapping is part of the semantics.

classes.name: option declared through a helper (mkPackageOption, mkEnableOption, shared option-generating function)
classes.semantic_property: declaration, default, type via helper arguments
classes.reason: The helper call's arguments define default and type. D may fail even when E holds; that is a derivation limitation.

classes.name: nested or submodule option (attrsOf or submodule instance)
classes.semantic_property: declaration, default, type at nested path
classes.reason: Same semantics as EC01-EC05 at a nested path.

classes.name: option declared with a dotted key inside an options block
classes.reason: Same semantics as the nested form; key spelling is not a semantic difference.

classes.name: build-time system check or derivation validation over module option values
classes.reason: Not an option branch predicate under README layer A. Added from the 569867 trace; v1 classed it under EC13 by judgment.

unresolved_product_decisions.question: Is a documentation-only change (EC06-EC08) in product scope?
unresolved_product_decisions.basis: README layer A has no documentation semantics.

unresolved_product_decisions.question: Are configuration-value assignments (EC11) a separate product mode or out of scope?
unresolved_product_decisions.status: CLOSED for reading (a): separate mode, not in E. Reading (b) still open.

unresolved_product_decisions.question: Are value-only behavioral options (no predicate) in E although oba cannot analyze them?
unresolved_product_decisions.basis: Under (a) layer A cannot witness them; under (b) they are E with an analyzer-scope outcome.

unresolved_product_decisions.question: Are predicate changes with foreign-only operands (EC12), warnings and assertions (EC13), and build checks (EC20) in E?
unresolved_product_decisions.basis: Reading (a) vs (b). 566007 (foreign-only operand), 566696 (warning), 569867 (build check) split the reading.

known_gaps: Attribute attribution by text heuristics is unreliable for multi-line Nix strings; an adjudicator must read the parsed or indented structure.
Helper-generated declarations (EC17) are E-eligible but their canonical path may be invisible to text search; this affects D, not E.
Configuration-dependent behavior beyond the module (EC11) is not evaluated by any class under reading (a).
